done_when: forge story new <KEY> "<title>" works for a story that has no spec: the story's own branch adds it to the roadmap, the plan's Why carries the problem, and the story gets one read loop and one approval; stories made from a spec work as today and specs stay optional. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body: Raise: Functional. For a spec-free story whose first task depends on another story's task, the new entry is committed only on `story/<KEY>` here. `task.start_base` uses the default branch for cross-story dependencies (`src/forge/task.py:288–296`), while `task.start` copies only the plan, read notes, and story state (`src/forge/task.py:280–283`). That task's pull request can therefore merge without the roadmap entry, leaving the completed story absent from the default branch's roadmap. The new test checks creation and approval but stops before task start.
findings.title: A dependent story's roadmap entry never reaches the default branch

why: A new story needs a spec, its own read loop, a confirmation and a roadmap fix before its plan can even start
